name: QPDF
listed_description: A tool and C++ library for content-preserving transformations of PDF files.
reason: No numeric comparison against any other tool. README, manual (design, overview) and release notes only compare qpdf with earlier qpdf versions (for example 'gains on the order of 20%' in developer benchmarks) and quote zopfli being about 100x slower than zlib; the performance_check script and qpdf/performance-test-files repo only time qpdf itself. qpdf does not render or extract text, so the guessed baselines poppler and PDFium do not apply, and a WebSearch snippet shows a Rust project (pdq) using qpdf as the baseline it beats, not the reverse. No head-to-head against MuPDF mutool, pdftk or Ghostscript found.

name: rnnoise
listed_description: Recurrent neural network for audio noise reduction.
reason: No numeric speed comparison against a named baseline in reachable sources. The repo README has no performance figures. Picovoice's noise-suppression-benchmark repo (raw README opened) gives RNNoise a real-time factor of 0.01 on a Ryzen 7 5900X, identical to Picovoice Koala (0.01), plus STOI 0.925 vs 0.915 for unprocessed audio (a quality figure, not speed). Search snippets of Valin's W3C talk give complexity of about 40 MFLOPS and 1.3% CPU on x86 and 14% on Raspberry Pi 3 for unoptimized C, with no baseline. The original paper (arXiv 1709.08243), jmvalin.ca demo and Mozilla Hacks post were blocked from this environment, so any Speex or other comparison there is unverified.

name: SDL
reason: No numeric comparison showing SDL faster than a named baseline. README, WhatsNew.txt and docs/README-migration.md contain no performance numbers. The libsdl-org issue #7634 (opened) shows SDL3 3.0.0 slower than SDL2 at startup before fixes (renderer creation 251-256 ms vs 69-72 ms, average FPS 37-38 vs 193-226 on Windows 11, Ryzen 7 5800X). The SFML-vs-SDL benchmark repo found has no results text, and a gamedev.net benchmark of SDL 1.2/2/3, HGE and SFML seen in search snippets was blocked so its numbers were not seen. SDL is a platform layer that other projects benchmark against rather than a faster replacement for a named incumbent.

name: SELA
reason: No benchmark or numbers anywhere reachable. README states the aim as simple with 'good enough compression ratios', lists 'Optimization' as TODO, and has no FLAC or other codec comparison; the sela-java companion README also has no performance or ratio statements. No third-party shootout including SELA found.

name: SoLoud
listed_description: Easy, portable audio engine for games.
reason: No performance comparison against FMOD, Wwise, SDL_mixer or OpenAL. README is three lines; docsrc intro, faq, backends, basics and voice docs describe features and ease of use and say SoLoud is not a replacement for FMOD or Wwise in tooling, with no speed numbers. A WebSearch for benchmarks found only feature comparison pages and an old README note that SoLoud has no assembler optimizations and uses point-sample resampling.
